 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE PRABHAT KUMAR SINGH  ORAL ORDER 3 10-04-2024 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the State.

2. Petitioner seeks regular bail in a case registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A,
328, 302/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Prosecution case, in brief, is that the daughter of the informant Chandrabati Devi (deceased) was married to the petitioner and after marriage, all the F.I.R. named accused persons including this petitioner used to harass her for dowry.
It is further alleged that this petitioner had illicit relationship with his sister-in-law and when the deceased protested, this petitioner assaulted and harassed her physically and mentally.
It is further alleged that all the accused persons conspired and gave poison to the deceased as a result of which she died during treatment.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.11767 of 2024(3)
dt.10-04-2024 informant is not an eye witness of the occurrence and this petitioner and his entire family has been made accused only on suspicion.
He next submits that the deceased died during treatment in presence of the family members of the informant which itself falsifies the entire prosecution case.

sentences.text: Learned A.P.P. for the State opposed the bail application and submitted that petitioner is husband of the deceased.

Inquest report shows that the deceased died due to poisoning and during investigation, sufficient material has come to show that this petitioner along with other accused persons poisoned the deceased resulting in her death.
6. Considering the nature of accusation and gravity of the offence, the regular bail application of the petitioner stands rejected.
(Prabhat Kumar Singh, J) Navya/-
